title: Effects of Prenatal PM<sub>10</sub> Exposure on Fetal Cardiovascular Malformations in Fuzhou, China: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.
authors: Liu CB, Hong XR, Shi M, Chen XQ, Huang HJ, Chen JH, Yang K, Chen SQ, Chen HQ, Kan HD, Sun QH.
quote: Results: PM10 levels were positively associated with the risks of atrial septal defect (aORs ranging from 1.29 to 2.17), patent ductus arteriosus [aORs=1.54, 1.63; 95% confidence intervals (CIs): 1.17, 2.23; 1.06, 3.24], overall fetal cardiovascular malformations (aOR=1.28; 95% CI: 1.03, 1.61), ventricular septal defect (aOR=1.19; 95% CI: 1.00, 1.43), and tetralogy of Fallot (aOR=1.44; 95% CI: 1.01, 2.19) in the various observed periods scaled by 10 d or 1 mo in the first and second gestation months.
